record.title: OpenAI manuscript claims the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2
record.summary: OpenAI’s 23-page manuscript claims that for every ν>2 there is a threshold Q(ν) such that |π−p/q|≥q^-ν for all integers p and q≥Q(ν), and concludes that π has irrationality exponent 2. If correct, this would sharply improve the prior upper bounds discussed in the paper. The threshold is ineffective; the manuscript does not prove a uniform c/q² lower bound or bounded continued-fraction partial quotients. OpenAI’s public family-017 note describes a Lean statement covering the exponent claim, but no independent build, semantic audit or number-theory review was performed here. Treat the theorem as claimed, not established.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI’s manuscript claims that the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2, with an ineffective threshold Q(ν) for each ν>2.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: OpenAI’s family-017 Lean scope note says its selected formal statement covers the irrationality-exponent result; the research desk has not rerun the build or independently audited paper-to-code semantics. MathVet separately reports a successful pinned build, closure check and Comparator run for this challenge.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The manuscript cites prior upper bounds <7.101862832357 and 7.103205334137…; source papers are the comparison baseline, not proof that the new result is correct.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: At pinned commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a, OAI/NumberTheory/PiExponent/Main.lean declares the exponent-equals-two theorem and a Flint–Hills summability helper. The separate ComparatorChallenges/PiExponent.lean contains sorry as a challenge scaffold; neither fact establishes that the proof builds or is mathematically correct.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: MathVet’s independent challenge-status record reports that family 017’s PiExponent statement matches the headline claim, builds successfully, has a successful closure check with one constant, no closure problems or shadowing, uses only the three standard Lean axioms, and passes Comparator on the reviewer laptop and an isolated Linux VM with real landrun. These checks establish the formal result under its encoded definitions, not the correctness of the manuscript proof or semantic correspondence.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent number-theory specialist review or reproduction was established.

An independent MathVet report now supplies a successful build, formal closure and Comparator run for PiExponent family 017 at the pinned challenge; its check is tied to OpenAI repository commit adc7f124, and MathVet reports the challenge unchanged at fd4aeeb2. the research desk has not reproduced these checks. The remaining unresolved issue is semantic correspondence between the manuscript proof, the Main.lean entrypoint/dependency closure, the scope note and the Comparator statement; in particular, Main.lean also declares a Flint–Hills helper while the scope note excludes that consequence. A current, unpinned OpenAI Math build/main.tex page exposes Theorem 1.1 with the same eventual inequality as the first conjunct of pinned Main.lean; this is statement-level alignment only, and current-path commit history was unavailable in this check.

brief.importance_rationale: If true, μ(π)=2 would settle a longstanding number-theory problem and substantially strengthen Diophantine approximation for π, with implications for related analytic questions. The claim is field-shifting in consequence; its truth remains unverified and must be evaluated separately.
limitations: The claim is from a first-party OpenAI manuscript; no number-theory specialist proof review or independent proof reproduction was established.
The threshold Q(ν) is non-effective; no explicit threshold is provided. The result does not claim a uniform c/q² bound or bounded continued-fraction partial quotients.

MathVet independently reports a successful build, closure check and Comparator acceptance for family 017 at the pinned challenge, including standard axioms and no shadowing. the research desk did not rerun those checks; MathVet’s family verdict is pre-referee.
Successful kernel checking establishes the encoded Lean theorem under its definitions, not that the natural-language manuscript is correct or faithfully represented by those definitions.
OpenAI’s scope note excludes the paper’s Flint–Hills convergence consequence from the selected statement. Main.lean also contains a Flint–Hills helper; their exact relationship remains unresolved.

The ComparatorChallenges/PiExponent.lean file contains sorry as a challenge scaffold and is distinct from the Main.lean proof entrypoint; the external status report records the challenge execution and main build separately.
The pinned TeX source was retrieved and its theorem text inspected; the PDF body itself did not load in the earlier activation.

technical.claimed_result: The manuscript claims μ(π)=2, equivalently that for every ν>2 there is Q(ν) such that all integer p and q≥Q(ν) satisfy |π−p/q|≥q^-ν.
technical.compute_or_cost: No model compute, compute cost, or human labor accounting specific to this theorem was verified in this review.
technical.demonstrated_result: MathVet's independently published challenge-status table reports that the PiExponent family-017 Comparator challenge builds, its transitive statement closure matches with one constant and no shadowing/problems, its axioms are the three standard Lean axioms, and Comparator accepted it on a reviewer laptop and an isolated Linux VM using real landrun. The status table's machine check is pinned to OpenAI commit adc7f124; MathVet reports the challenge was byte-identical at later commit fd4aeeb2. the research desk did not rerun these checks. This demonstrates an externally reported machine-checked formal theorem under the encoded statement; it does not validate the mathematical manuscript or prove semantic correspondence.
technical.implementation_status: At OpenAI commit adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a, OAI/NumberTheory/PiExponent/Main.lean declares the eventual lower-bound and exponent-equals-two theorem plus a Flint–Hills helper. MathVet's independent status record reports a successful build and Comparator run for the separate family-017 challenge, with closure and standard-axiom checks; it reports the challenge unchanged at fd4aeeb2. the research desk did not rerun these checks. The selected theorem's paper-to-code semantic correspondence remains open.
technical.mechanism: The manuscript presents an interpolation/determinant argument to derive an eventual lower bound |π−p/q|≥q^-ν for each fixed ν>2. Its formalization note identifies a selected Lean theorem for the irrationality-exponent statement.
technical.novelty: The paper claims a major reduction in the upper bound for π’s irrationality exponent, from about 7.10 to 2.
technical.regime: Classical irrationality exponent of π, with a non-effective threshold depending on each ν>2. The result does not imply a uniform constant c/q² or bounded partial quotients.
technical.reproducibility: MathVet reports a successful build, dependency-closure check and Comparator acceptance for PiExponent family 017 at the pinned OpenAI commit adc7f124; its later challenge table is generated against fd4aeeb2 and its changelog says the earlier challenge statement is byte-identical. This is an independent reported machine check, not an the research desk reproduction. The manuscript-to-Lean semantic correspondence and mathematical proof remain independently unreviewed.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper cites prior upper bounds 7.103205334137… (Zeilberger–Zudilin, 2020) and <7.101862832357 (Bai, 2026). The new claim, if valid, is a large improvement; these baselines are themselves published mathematical results and are not independently audited here.

brief.title: OpenAI manuscript claims the irrationality exponent of π is exactly 2
brief.why_it_matters: An independently verified exponent of 2 for π would settle a long-standing Diophantine-approximation question and affect related number-theory results. The implication is unusually large, while the current evidence remains an unreviewed first-party paper and formalization claim.
